clue.text: Sending down of student from showing little industry

definitions.text: Sending down of student from showing little industry

indicators.note: sending a student down means expelling them, so the student letter is removed from the word that follows 'from'

parts.note: slacking means idling and showing little effort
L, the learner plate, stands for a student or learner

explanation.surface: A university expels an undergraduate for laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: Sending down is the British university term for expelling a student; the whole clue both defines the answer and builds it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sent down for slacking is a dismissal, and dismissal is a synonym of getting the sack.

clue.text: Island with old vessel at the point

parts.note: S, south, is one of the compass points
Noah's ark is the ancient vessel of Genesis

explanation.surface: An island where an ancient ship sits at the headland.
explanation.walkthrough: SARK is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is a small Channel Island, so this is an example of the category named.

clue.text: Advantage of Ken's congestion charge?

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, Mayor of London, introduced the congestion charge; read playfully, the capital city gains from that levy

explanation.surface: Asking what good the London mayor's road charge does.
explanation.walkthrough: The real term is a tax on profits from selling assets; the pun splits it as the capital (London) gaining from a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally names a levy on asset profits, here reread as the profit London makes from a levy.

clue.text: Disregard devastated region

indicators.note: something devastated is wrecked, so the letters of the next word are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Turning a blind eye to a ruined district.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to pay it no attention, a direct synonym of the verb answer.

clue.text: Asking to fit back to front seal

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is brought round from the back to the front

explanation.surface: A request to put a seal the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' moves the final G of ASKING to the start; 'to fit' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaskin is a piece of packing used to seal a joint, a variant of gasket.

clue.text: Old peasants offer sleeping accommodation to the navy

parts.note: a cot is a small bed or bunk
tars are sailors, collectively the navy

explanation.surface: Cottagers once gave beds to visiting sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottars were Scottish farm labourers who rented a cottage, peasants of former times.

clue.text: Put to death through cash dealing in China

indicators.note: one piece is run through the middle of the other, so it sits inside
cash being dealt out is shuffled, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: to hang someone is to execute them

explanation.surface: An execution carried out over money transactions in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing' scrambles the letters of cash into CSHA, and 'through' runs the execution word inside them. Changsha is the capital of Hunan province.
explanation.definitionFit: Changsha is a city in China, the capital of Hunan province, so the clue words point to a place there.

clue.text: Reference works showing smash hit about hairy man — redhead

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the outside of the rest
to smash something breaks it up, so the letters of hit are rearranged

parts.note: Esau is the hairy man of Genesis, brother of Jacob
the head of the word red is its first letter, R

explanation.surface: Books about a hit record by a shaggy ginger fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smash' turns HIT into THI, which goes 'about' ESAU plus R.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesaurus is a reference book of synonyms; the Latin plural names several such works.

clue.text: AS early …

parts.note: the clue's two letters read as A followed by the first letter, or head, of the word schedule

explanation.surface: A fragment hinting something is premature.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, would be a instruction to write A then the head of SCHEDULE, which gives the clue's AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something early means doing it before the planned time, an idiom for being in advance of the timetable.

clue.text: One could be on hand long ago

definitions.text: One could be on hand long ago

parts.words: One could be on hand long ago
parts.note: a ring worn on the finger to mark a wedding anniversary of twenty-five years, a marriage made long ago

explanation.surface: Something that might have been at hand in olden days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on hand' looks like 'available' but means literally on the hand, worn on a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring marking twenty-five years of marriage is worn on the hand and commemorates a wedding long past.

clue.text: Porn one can be devastated to see

indicators.note: letters that can be devastated may be wrecked and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: Smut that a person might be shocked to come across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' looks like the verb to view, but it is the noun: a bishop's seat. RIPON is a cathedral city in Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon has a cathedral and is the seat of a bishop, which is what a see is.

clue.text: "Fish in heaving water" — dispenser's instruction

indicators.note: the fish is placed inside the water

parts.note: a swell is the heaving motion of the sea
hake is a food fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in rough sea, followed by a pharmacist's directions.
explanation.walkthrough: A dispenser here is a pharmacist, who labels medicine bottles with this direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Pharmacists label liquid medicines with this direction to mix the contents before use.

clue.text: Name given at registration — a feature of old cars

definitions.meaning: a handle is slang for a name, and the one you start with is the first name registered at birth
the crank inserted at the front of a vintage car to turn the engine over

explanation.surface: A registered name and a part found on vintage vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a crank for starting an early car engine and, playfully, a first name or handle.

clue.text: "Christ rose transfigured", they sing

indicators.note: something transfigured has its form changed, so these letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: An Easter hymn sung by the people who perform it.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of a church choir are singers, so they are the ones who sing.

clue.text: Gap left by removing the head from all parts

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken away

parts.note: a whole is the thing with all its parts together

explanation.surface: A gap left after decapitating everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole is an opening or gap, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One in service could be hurt by fire

indicators.note: the letters of the following words could be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Someone at a service might get burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: The service is a church service; 'by' is a link joining the two fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: A thurifer is the server who carries the censer of incense during a church service.

clue.text: Outer clothing for the masses

parts.note: the masses are not the general public but celebrations of Mass, for which a priest wears an outer vestment

explanation.surface: Coats for ordinary people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the masses' suggests the common people; it means church Masses.
explanation.definitionFit: A chasuble is the sleeveless outermost vestment a priest wears to celebrate Mass.

clue.text: US marine served in Iraq in former times

indicators.note: food that is served is dished up, here the letters being dished up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An American marine did a tour of duty in Iraq years ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumer was an ancient civilisation in southern Mesopotamia, now Iraq, so its people belong there long ago.

clue.text: Extend every member in crushing defeat

indicators.note: the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: a rout is an overwhelming defeat
each refers to every member of a group

explanation.surface: Spreading a loss across all players in a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an arm or offer help is a synonym of this phrasal verb.

clue.text: Examine for cold in hospital

indicators.note: the cold letter is placed inside the hospital

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a kind of hospital
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Being checked over for a chill while hospitalised.
explanation.definitionFit: To scan something is to look it over closely, a synonym of examine.

clue.text: Artist's pictures cherished for surreal content

indicators.note: the content of the words is what they hold inside, so the answer lies within them

explanation.surface: A painter's treasured works are prized for their dreamlike quality.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (is); 'surreal' fits the artist known for impossible drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: M. C. Escher was a Dutch graphic artist famous for impossible constructions.

clue.text: Smoke and end result takes a turn for what's dramatic

indicators.note: turning round means the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cigar is something to smoke

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Lighting up and its consequences become serious.
explanation.walkthrough: CIGAR plus T (the end of 'result') makes CIGART, which 'takes a turn' to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic drama is a branch of theatre, so the adjective describes what is dramatic in that sense.

clue.text: Novel left setter in disarray

parts.note: sinister is Latin and heraldic for left

indicators.note: being in disarray means the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A book abandoned by a disorganised compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister Street is a 1913 novel by Compton Mackenzie.
explanation.definitionFit: Compton Mackenzie wrote this 1913 novel, so it names one specific work of fiction.

clue.text: Outdoor slippers

parts.note: not house footwear but things worn on the feet to slide across snow

explanation.surface: Indoor footwear worn outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slippers' suggests soft shoes; it means things that slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Skis are worn on the feet outdoors and slide over snow, playfully called things that slip.

clue.text: Settle attempt to supplant no good in English

indicators.note: one piece supplants, or takes the place of, another inside the word
the swap happens inside the word that follows, English

parts.note: taken as the full word
a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: Trying to oust incompetence in England to settle things.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish is to settle or set up firmly, a synonym.

clue.text: Composer's good fortune

parts.note: luck is fortune

explanation.surface: A composer's lucky break.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (is). Gluck was an 18th-century German opera composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Christoph Willibald Gluck was an 18th-century opera composer, so this is an instance of a composer.

clue.text: Number observed to contain 10 in it

indicators.note: the first word holds the rest within it

parts.note: seen means observed

indicators.note: the ten goes inside the next word

parts.note: taken as written
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A figure was seen to have ten in it.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes 'in' the word it to give IXT, and the word for observed is said 'to contain' that run.
explanation.definitionFit: Sixteen is a whole number, so it is an example of a number.

clue.text: Dodgy practices in sport

definitions.meaning: a fast indoor game played with racquets against walls, an ancestor of squash

explanation.surface: Underhand dealings in the world of games.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fraudulent schemes and an old court game, the forerunner of squash.
